title: Tenant-aware SLO concession window, hedged fallback, and rapid circuit-reset hotfix
author: Nikhil Patel
description: Motivation: Under multi-tenant surge conditions the SLO enforcer would hard-open circuits at region-level too aggressively, evicting low-volume tenants and causing cascade failures for mid-priority workloads. Additionally, an intermittent race in runtime/kv/cache_manager caused a double-free when rapid circuit reset rehydrated caches, producing OOMs and duplicated responses on the hot path. This PR introduces three coordinated changes: (1) a tenant-aware SLO concession window that grants short, decaying concession budgets per tenant based on historical p50/p95 and tenant priority so we avoid global hard-open decisions; (2) a hedged fallback path that issues a parallel request to a slower but stable model variant when tail latency or queueing crosses configured thresholds; (3) a targeted hotfix that serializes cache rehydration and makes cache insert/remove idempotent to eliminate the double-free race. All features are behind feature flags (runtime.flags.tenant_slo_concession and runtime.flags.hedged_fallback) defaulted off. Implementation notes: concession allocator maintains per-tenant sliding window counters, decays budgets with exponential backoff, exposes concession tokens on request context for the router and enforcer to consume; hedged fallback forks a low-priority replica request with deduplication token and cost accounting; cache_manager now uses a lightweight refcount + CAS-style replace to guarantee idempotent rehydration. Testing: added unit tests for allocator and cache invariants, added integration scenarios to perf-canary showing a ~30% reduction in tenant-wide evictions under 2x arrival spikes and a 12% decrease in p99 tail for affected tenants with hedging enabled. Rollout plan: gated canary rollout (5% -> 25% -> 100%), monitor error-rate, tenant SLOs and memory headroom; automatic rollback triggers on >0.5% absolute increase in error-rate for any high-priority tenant or memory OOM spikes. Rollback: toggle feature flag to off and revert if rollback automation does not stabilize. Related work: ENG-5423 (SLO concession design), ENG-5498 (hedged fallback UX), SUP-2114 (incident tracking OOM).

review_comments: Elena Park: Please add a short doc explaining concession semantics and tenant priority mapping before merge — we need operators to understand tradeoffs.
Marcus Li: I reproduced the OOM on staging; the CAS-style insert fixes it for me. Can you confirm the refcount never underflows? Add an assertion in debug builds.
Samira Khan: Hedging looks good, but ensure cost accounting ties into per-tenant billing reports (we don't want hidden double-charges).

Nikhil Patel (author): Added operator doc under observability and a debug-only assert for refcount underflow. Billing tie-in is added as a metric (slo.hedge_extra_tokens) and will be surfaced in the console dashboard.
Marcus Li: Approved after assertions and doc additions verified in staging.
release_notes: Introduce tenant-aware SLO concession windows and hedged fallback to reduce tenant eviction and tail latency; fix KV cache race that could cause OOMs and duplicate responses. Rollout is gated behind feature flags.
